text:
…turned the wheel of the Dharma that tames;
it is fitting here to call you Wheel-holder.
Your speech is excellent and pleasing,
and you have always wholly abandoned childish beings.
Pleasing, excellent, sweet to the ear,
delightful, sweet and harmonious,
it satisfies the mind and bestows bliss:
this the Buddhas truly call "Mañju."
Even those Tathāgatas, with all their distinction,
do not fathom your power;
nor do their sons who have entered the grounds,
beyond the world, numbering ten.
Nor can you, lord of gods, distinguished in the world,
know the excellent Sage.
Those of form and the formless, those dwelling on the earth,
the gods of desire, and humans born of mind,
those who have attained yogic accomplishment, and in the world
all the distinguished ones, likewise the lords of men:
there is no being
by whom his greatness could be known.
One who fully knows this greatness of yours
is a Buddha who thoroughly knows what "Mañju" means.
That you are designated "Mañjuśrī" —
this name of yours was given by the Victors of old.
Your name having been so designated, of the Buddhas
past, future and present…
Whoever, undistracted, one-pointed, with pure mind,
hears your name within the assembly,
thereby attains knowledge and peace here,
and at the end of existence may attain supreme awakening in particular.
All mantras without exception will be accomplished,
and the birthplaces of beings…
…entered. As soon as the Blessed One Śākyamuni had entered absorption, from the ūrṇā hair between his brows there issued rays of light blue, yellow, white, crimson and crystal-coloured. They illuminated this entire buddha-field and illuminated other world-systems as well, and in a moment they outshone and summoned all the planets and constellations. Having summoned them, they set each properly in its own place; and having drawn them by the Buddha's blessing into that circle of the assembly, the rays disappeared into that very ūrṇā hair of the Blessed One. All the planets, constellations and stars, their light extinguished, wretched and afraid, went for refuge to the Blessed One Śākyamuni and remained with palms joined; thus they trembled violently and fell to the ground again and again. Then the Blessed One Śākyamuni, in order to take into his care all the planets, constellations and stars, the learned, and beings possessed of the understanding of childish people, spoke: "Friends, assemblies of gods together with humans, listen! In the varied world, beings depend upon karma itself. Whatever is the manifestly accomplished vajra body of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and whatever the world with its gods and asuras, many…
